`if`/`else` branches on a condition; `for` loops repeat code over a sequence. Loops are common in R, though vectorized code (like Lesson 2) is usually faster and more idiomatic.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>Before you run the code below: <code>grade_of()</code> checks conditions top to bottom and stops at the first match. For a score of <code>82</code>, which branch fires first — <code>&gt;= 90</code>, <code>&gt;= 80</code>, or <code>&gt;= 70</code>?</p>
</div>
```

Edit the code below if you like, then press **Run Code** to check your answer.

```{webr-r}
grade_of <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 90) "A"
  else if (score >= 80) "B"
  else if (score >= 70) "C"
  else "F"
}

for (s in c(95, 82, 71, 40)) {
  cat("Score", s, "->", grade_of(s), "\n")
}
```
